newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks end up led by blue chips.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks end up led by blue chips.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed up in active Monday trade where late foreign buying of highly capitalised blue chips played a major role, brokers said.

The all share index closed 5.53 points up at 628.64. Price gains led losses by 38 to 12. Blue chips Development Finance and John Keells Holdings rose 10.25 rupees and one rupee to 285 and 185, respectively.
"It was good for a Monday when investors are usually wary," said Sanjeeva Gunewardena a trader at Commercial Stock Brokers.
The active start to the week came on the momentum generated from last week's budget, he said.
Turnover was 23.6 million rupees on 919,977 shares.
Foreign buying amounted to 7.2 million rupees and comprised 14,000 Development Finance and 10,100 John Keells Holdings.
"There is some new foreign buying being seen after good corporate results for the quarter to September 30, and last week's budget," said a broker at CT Smith.
Brokers said they expected the upward trend of the index to continue, but cautioned that a fast rise would only result in quick profit-taking.
"Even today's rise is too fast. I think the ideal is three points a day," said Gunewardena of Commercial stock Brokers.
